memo.verdict: Progress to Early-Stage rather than park. Bullish on the business and the price; conviction medium-low, a working hypothesis. The gate does not close: no D or F on management (B), business quality (A), predictability (B) or trackability (C); the D on broad mediocrity is not a gate item and is argued to be a statement about timing, since four of its eight Ds are momentum and sentiment readings the pattern carries by construction. Not deploy, because the two pinned momentum ratings say the market has not confirmed, the case's crispness depends on one more half-year, and the return at the bar depends on a re-rating. Not park, because the downside on a 16 percent compounder with no debt at the floor of its multiple range is bounded in a way most C cases are not, the three-year return without any re-rating is 12 percent a year, and every one of the six concerns has a dated test inside twelve months (the Q3 update in late October 2026; the H2 results on 10-Feb-27; the finance-director appointment; the acquisitions' first disclosed revenue). Move to deploy on: organic growth at or above 20 percent constant currency at the Q3 update and the H2 print with the take rate at or above 16 basis points, and technical momentum moving to B (price above a rising 200-day average, now EUR 1,000.6). Move to park on: organic growth below 18 percent for two quarters, EMEA below 12 percent, the take rate below 15.5 basis points, or an admission of Shopify-driven volume loss.
case: Adyen is a top-decile payments compounder whose shares fell 40 percent in twelve months on a February 2026 guidance reset (2026 narrowed to 20 to 22 percent from low-to-mid 20s; the 55 percent margin target pushed from 2026 to 2028; the shares -21 to 22 percent that day), a commoditisation narrative, an AI-related sector sell-off and a surprise finance-director exit, leaving the 24-month-forward multiple at 15.5x, the lowest in the stock's history, while the business kept growing net revenue at 21 percent constant currency and converting 86 percent of EBITDA to cash. At EUR 870.0 the market is paying for the bear case (low-teens EPS growth, a margin capped near 50 percent, no re-rating), so the shares return about 12 percent a year over three years with no re-rating at all, and about 24 percent a year over eighteen months if three more prints confirm organic growth at or above 20 percent and the market pays 21x rather than 15x. The case turns on that re-rating, the leg least in the company's control.

The change is the company's own cycle turning, and it is modest. The Cash App and eBay roll-offs lapped; Q2 2026 net revenue +22 percent constant currency from 20 percent in Q1, 1 percent ahead of the Visible Alpha consensus of 21 percent; Digital from 9 percent constant currency in Q4 2025 (against a consensus expectation of 13 percent) to 13 in Q1 and 16 in Q2; Q2 volume EUR 421.7 billion +26 percent; take rate flat quarter on quarter at 16.2 basis points; FX from a 2 percent headwind in H1 to a 1 percent tailwind in H2. The revenue cycle is B; every other external force is C or D: demand C (structural digitisation: US and UK e-commerce +11 percent, eurozone +5 percent in Q2 2026, and the eurozone carries 55 percent of net revenue; European card penetration 44 percent in 2019 to 77 percent in 2025; Adyen about 11 percent of global e-commerce), competition D (Stripe USD 1.9 trillion +34 percent and about 50 percent of the Fortune 100; Checkout.com USD 300 billion +64 percent; the Stripe and Advent USD 60.50 per share, USD 53 billion offer for PayPal rejected 15-Jul-26; take rate 16.8 to 16.2 basis points year on year; RFPs a race to the bottom; countervailing: Braintree slowed from 30 to 5 percent as it priced for value, Shopify moving European volume from Stripe toward Adyen, no European enterprise churn to Checkout.com in 2026), disruption C (Adyen Agentic June 2026 and the x402 Foundation against Mastercard and Visa aiming for 100 percent tokenisation by 2030, which narrows the authorisation-rate edge; agentic revenue not observable before late 2027), regulation C (shifting from interchange, passed through under Interchange++, to network fees and cross-border corridors where 2 to 4 percent FX markups sit; a mild headwind), supply C (server scarcity managed by capex at about 7 percent of net revenue in FY2026, normalising after), macro C (discretionary and travel exposure against a natural hedge; a 10 percent USD fall cuts net revenue EUR 63.8 million and EPS EUR 0.82), catch-all D (a Stripe-owned PayPal, possible not probable). External forces C.

Internal forces C: two strong (strategy change B: a complete financial operating system, EUR 750 million for Talon.One and USD 335 million for Orb under an incubator model, adding about 1 point to FY2026 growth, the first change of kind in the company's history; new products B: Agentic, Intelligent Money Movement, Uplift and Dynamic Identification at +0.9 percentage points conversion, Issuing volume eightfold and Capital loans doubled in 2025 and again in H1 2026, about 1 point of 2026 growth). The rest: other leaders C (replacement not reinforcement), guidance raised C (the 1-point raise wholly inorganic, a screen false positive; margin guidance down 1 point), standards C (discipline real, attrition 15 percent from 13.8 to 14, senior product tenure below 2.5 years, decisions slower), new geographies C (North America over 600 FTEs and under 5 percent card penetration; Uber in 40 new markets), acquisitions C (coherent, untested; Morgan Stanley reads them as possibly a defensive reaction), balance sheet C (EUR 1 billion used, nothing returned, cash EUR 12.39 billion), chief executive D (no change; reappointed to 2030), price rises D (take rate falling through tiering; defended by value), shareholder returns D (nil dividend FY2019 to FY2025, no buyback, near-term returns "highly unlikely"), perimeter reduction D (none), catch-all C (named wins OpenAI, Toast, Uber across 70 countries, Starbucks 943 stores, Lufthansa, GOV.UK Pay 1,000 services from Stripe; the cohort disclosure newly quantified). The screen rule is not met; the red-flag check is clean except the one-off guidance rise. 'Change Forces' C; the re-acceleration has travelled four of six layers (choices, actions, key operating metrics, financial statements), not the sell-side's estimates or the share price; the M&A is at the actions layer with no output.
counter_case: At its strongest: Adyen is a commoditising incumbent, not an oversold compounder, and the cause for concern is not transient. Card acquiring is commoditising from underneath: Mastercard and Visa aim for 100 percent network tokenisation by 2030, which flattens the authorisation-rate edge that earned Adyen its premium and which a former head of Adyen's North America partnerships says has already narrowed its technological lead; orchestration layers cut switching costs by making routing changes simple; Stripe matches the licences over time; and expert testimony says the single platform of the public narrative is three back-ends and a modular monolith with substantial technical debt. Europe is mature: Adyen already holds about 32 percent of European e-commerce excluding Amazon and about 50 percent of the enterprise segment, EMEA (55 percent of net revenue) slowed from 21 to 15 percent in a year, eurozone e-commerce grows 5 percent, and Shopify's Shop Pay on Stripe rails is taking European enterprise checkout, at about 9 percent of European retail e-commerce with over 30 brand migrations on Rothschild & Co Redburn's channel checks. On that reading core Digital net revenue compounds at 8 percent to 2028, the take rate compresses below 15.5 basis points as Stripe and Checkout.com discount for logos and RFPs run to the bottom, the margin is structurally capped below 50 percent, the company's first M&A at 12.5x recurring revenue is a defensive reaction to a saturating organic market (Morgan Stanley's phrase), the finance-director exit after two years of resets is a tell, and the operator is becoming bureaucratic and slow with senior turnover through the former COO, the former CTO, platform heads and the North America president and attrition at 15 percent. EPS then grows in the low teens, the multiple compresses to 16x on a lower EPS, and the fair value trends towards Jefferies' bear value of EUR 539 (-38 percent); an optically cheap valuation rarely presents a floor when terminal-value concerns persist, and the sector's floor (about 9x EV to EBITDA; on unrestricted cash Adyen trades at about 15x consensus FY2026 EBITDA, not a trough) sits below where Adyen trades on a cash-adjusted basis, so a 20 to 30 percent mark-to-market fall on the multiple alone is possible. The evidence: Digital grew 9 percent constant currency in Q4 2025 against consensus of 13; the take rate fell from 17.1 to 16.2 basis points in three quarters; the company missed four of nine quarters since 2024 and reset in 2023, 2025 and 2026; the concern has now lasted through three years of resets; the Q2 2026 acceleration coincides with the easiest comparison, the lapping of the Cash App and eBay roll-offs; financial income is about 20 percent of pre-tax profit and rate-sensitive; and the risks research names three masking mechanisms (mix-driven take-rate beats hiding volume loss, interest income hiding core deceleration, constant-currency growth hiding unit-economics deterioration) that could make the clearing look real when it is not, and makes that FALSE FRIEND profile its dominant outcome. On the pattern: the wisdom-of-crowd red flag is present, the case-outputs count trips at eight, the framework's own arithmetic finds 46 percent of scoped attributes at C, and the earnings momentum pin at D and the technical pin at C say the market has looked and not agreed. Against the 'Investment Case' rating from the other side: a top-decile business at a 0th-percentile multiple with organic growth re-accelerating is 'OSHQC CfC Clearing' in its purest form, the Cs are the sector's Cs and not the company's, valuation is pinned A, 74 percent of ratings are Buy with a mean target 61 percent above the price, and a C will cause Richard to pass on the best quality-at-a-trough opportunity in the universe.

The record's concessions: European maturity is real and the path carries it (EMEA 13 to 15 percent; group growth slowing a point a year); the take rate will not rise; the architecture question is open; the multiple's floor is not a bound; the masking mechanisms are real enough to monitor; the operator's steering is a real weakness; the C on the 'Investment Case' is the framework's arithmetic applied as written and moves to B territory if the H2 2026 print delivers.
triggers: To deploy: organic growth at or above 20 percent constant currency at the Q3 2026 update (late October) and the H2 2026 print (10-Feb-27) with the take rate at or above 16 basis points; technical momentum to B (price above a rising 200-day average, now EUR 1,000.6). To park: organic growth below 18 percent for two quarters; EMEA below 12 percent; the take rate below 15.5 basis points; an admission of Shopify-driven volume loss. Invalidate levels: organic growth below 18 percent for two quarters; take rate below 15.5 sustained; EBITDA margin below 53 percent at end-FY2027 excluding one-offs; EMEA below 12 percent for two quarters; a company admission of Shopify-driven volume loss; a single-stack outage attributed to integration. Alarm levels: organic growth below 20 percent in a quarter; take rate below 16.0; FY2026 margin below 51 percent; a named European enterprise loss to Shop Pay; the ECB deposit rate 100 basis points lower; EMEA below 13 percent; dilution above 1.5 points or acquisition revenue below EUR 25 million for FY2026; no finance-director appointment by mid-2027; a signed Stripe-PayPal deal; net hires below 400 or above 800 a year. Other warnings: volume growth below 18 percent; Platforms below 30 percent; top-300 share above 65 percent; merchant interest income above 8 percent of net revenue. What moves the ratings: if H2 2026 delivers organic growth at or above 20 percent with the margin at guidance, four of the eight Ds (upgrades, earnings momentum, the two concern counts) and several Cs (clearing evidence, named concern, revisions) move up and the case count moves to B territory; 'Investment Setup' B; Headline Rating 4 C if the print does not confirm. Delivery without re-rating for two prints would say the multiple is industry-driven. Open items: the three-back-ends architecture question bearing on integration; the permanent finance director; the Stripe and Advent approach to PayPal; the framework's track record and lessons files and the Wisdom Library and the live thematics file, none among the inputs, to be revisited at Early-Stage; the acquisitions' first disclosed revenue against segment consensus of EUR 30.3 million for FY2026; whether the FALSE FRIEND masking mechanisms show in the three diagnostics (volume against take rate; core acquiring growth against interest income; constant-currency against reported); the rate path for financial income (the drop-through sensitivity takes the three-year return to a C on its own); whether the market values the cash pile as free or only the about EUR 5.0 billion unrestricted.
